name: Pepper Jelly

ingredients.name: low-sugar powdered pectin, such as Ball or Sure-Jell

instructions.primary_message: Stem and seed the red bell peppers. Stem and seed the Fresno chiles. Stem, seed, and finely chop the green bell peppers. Stem, seed, and finely chop the jalapeño chiles.
instructions.secondary_message:
5 large red bell peppers, divided
3 Fresno chiles, divided
2 large green bell peppers
2 medium jalapeño chiles

instructions.primary_message: Thoroughly wash 6 (1/2-pint-size) canning jars and their lids. If you plan to process the jelly for shelf-stable storage, sterilize the jars as described in our canning guide.

Coarsely chop 2 red bell peppers and 2 Fresno chiles, and place in bowl of a food processor. Pulse until very finely chopped, about 12 pulses, scraping down sides of bowl as needed. Transfer mixture to a large stockpot or Dutch oven. Using a knife, finely chop remaining 3 red bell peppers and the remaining Fresno chile; transfer to Dutch oven with peppers. Add green bell peppers, jalapeño chiles, and salt to Dutch oven.
Cook, covered, over medium heat until peppers are completely softened, about 8 minutes.

Uncover and simmer, stirring occasionally, until most of the liquid has evaporated, about 5 minutes. Stir in sugar and vinegar and bring mixture to a full boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to a simmer. Stir in pectin until dissolved, return heat to medium-high, and bring to a full rolling boil. As soon as mixture reaches a full boil, cook for 1 minute, then remove from heat. Let stand for 5 minutes. Using a metal spoon, carefully scrape any foam or scum from surface of jelly. Transfer jelly into prepared canning jars, leaving 0.5-cm space at the top. Using wet paper towels or a kitchen towel, wipe any jelly from the rims.

For short-term storage: Let jelly cool to room temperature, about 30 minutes. Screw on lids, and refrigerate until set, at least 12 hours. Jelly can be stored for up to 1 month in refrigerator. When ready to serve, stir jelly to distribute peppers evenly.

For long-term storage: While jelly is still hot, screw on tops until finger-tip tight (do not over-tighten). Place a canning rack in bottom of a large stockpot. Fill with water, and bring to a boil over high heat. Carefully lower jars into pot. Return water to boil over high; cover and boil for 10 minutes. Off-heat, let jars sit in water for 5 minutes. Using canning tongs, carefully remove jars from water. Jelly can be stored at room temperature for up to 1 year; refrigerate after opening and use within 3 weeks. When ready to serve, stir jelly to distribute peppers evenly.

description: This easy-to-make pepper jelly is the perfect Southern accompaniment for cheese, crackers, sandwiches, and much more.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 13 hr.

Notes: This recipe was developed using low-sugar pectin; do not substitute other types of pectin unless you know how to properly adjust the recipe. We recommend using either the low-sugar pectin from Ball or brand or Sure-Jell rather than other brands (the brand Pomona's, in particular, did not work like Ball or Sure-Jell in our tests).Jelly served cold will have a firmer texture. Bring to room temperature if a looser texture is desired.

Make-ahead and storage: Unprocessed jelly can be refrigerated for 1 month.
Processed (heat-treated) jelly can be stored in a cool, dark place for up to 1 year. After opening, refrigerate and use within 3 weeks.
When ready to serve, stir jelly to distribute peppers evenly.
author: Laila Ibrahim
